title: What If a Giant Solar Storm Hit Astronauts on the Moon?

scenes.text: What if the Sun blasted astronauts walking on the Moon? It almost happened.
In August 1972, between Apollo 16 and Apollo 17, a huge solar storm erupted from a giant sunspot.
The Moon has no air to stop the particles. Outside a spacecraft, the dose rate reached about 241 rem an hour.
NASA's Francis Cucinotta estimated a moonwalker could absorb around 400 rem. Half of people dosed above 300 rem would die within sixty days without care.
Inside the Apollo command module, the dose would have dropped to under 35 rem. Shelter mattered.
Nobody was on the Moon that week. Apollo 17 landed four months later, and a few millimeters of aluminum can shield against such storms.

description:
What if a giant solar storm hit astronauts on the Moon?
It nearly happened in August 1972, and a moonwalker could have absorbed around 400 rem, but nobody was up there.
What should we run through next?
